formulations.statement: Conservation of energy: for an isolated system the total energy — summed over all forms (kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, nuclear, ...) — remains constant in time; energy transforms between forms but is neither created nor destroyed. Historical line: Mayer (1842), Joule (1843), Helmholtz (1847, 'Über die Erhaltung der Kraft'); standard statement per Halliday, Resnick, Walker 12th ed., Ch 8.

formulations.event: First statement of energy conservation (work-heat equivalence)
Über die Erhaltung der Kraft — formal statement of energy conservation

formulations.statement: Newton's second law of motion: the net external force on a system equals the time rate of change of its total linear momentum, ΣF = dp/dt; for constant mass this reduces to F = m a. Valid in classical (non-relativistic) mechanics in inertial reference frames. Stated by Isaac Newton as Lex II in Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687); standard modern formulation per Halliday, Resnick, Walker 12th ed., Ch 5.
